t: MoC-System: Efficient Fault Tolerance for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Training
pb: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs have model parameter counts far exceeding dense models of equivalent compute cost, making checkpoint-based fault tolerance extremely expensive in terms of checkpoint size, write bandwidth, and recovery time for distributed training at >10k node scale.
me: MoC-System exploits the sparse activation pattern of MoE models: only a subset of experts is activated per token, so most expert parameters are not updated in any given training step. The system uses a Model-on-Checkpoint (MoC) approach that selectively checkpoints only the experts that were actually updated (activated) during a training step, avoiding checkpointing dormant expert parameters. This is combined with distributed checkpoint orchestration to overlap checkpoint I/O with forward/backward computation and expert-parallel sharding to minimize per-node checkpoint volume.
nv: Exploiting MoE sparse activation to checkpoint only updated (active) experts per step, drastically reducing checkpoint size and I/O without sacrificing fault recovery correctness.

mx.other: reduced checkpoint overhead for MoE models; specific numbers not in abstract

th: sparse-activation-aware fault tolerance for MoE LLM training

t: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
pb: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs have very large total parameter counts that exceed the VRAM of commodity GPUs, forcing weight offloading to CPU memory or NVMe, which creates severe I/O bottlenecks and low GPU utilization during batch inference.
me: MoE-Lightning introduces CGOPipe (CPU-GPU-I/O Pipelining) with paged weight management: expert weights are stored in pages that are streamed between CPU memory and GPU memory in a pipeline overlapping expert computation with prefetching of the next expert's weights. A Hierarchical Roofline Model (HRM) performance model guides policy selection by predicting throughput as a function of batch size, GPU memory, CPU memory, and I/O bandwidth. The system supports multi-GPU configurations for even larger models (Mixtral 8x22B, DBRX) on 2-4 T4 GPUs.
nv: CGOPipe: a CPU-GPU-I/O pipeline with paged expert weights, guided by a Hierarchical Roofline Model, that achieves near-peak offloading throughput with significantly less CPU memory than prior work.

mx.speedup: 10.3x throughput over state-of-the-art offloading-enabled LLM inference (Mixtral 8x7B on single T4 16GB GPU)
mx.other: 2-3x less CPU memory at throughput upper bound

th: CPU-GPU-IO pipeline for high-throughput MoE inference on memory-constrained GPUs

t: Hopps: Leveraging Sparsity to Accelerate Automata Processing
pb: Automata processing (AP) workloads execute many finite state machines (FSMs) in parallel over streaming symbol data, but existing AP accelerators suffer poor utilization because most FSMs are inactive (in a non-matching state) for any given input symbol. The irregular, state-dependent activation pattern makes it hard to exploit spatial parallelism efficiently.
me: Hopps exploits the observation that only a sparse subset of FSMs transition on each input symbol. It uses a sparsity-aware representation that tracks only active states across all FSMs and a compressed activation bitmap to skip idle FSMs entirely during each symbol step. The architecture couples this with a tiled SRAM storage layout so that state-transition tables for active FSMs are fetched in bursts, reducing off-chip memory traffic proportional to the active-FSM fraction.
nv: Hopps is the first AP accelerator to exploit cross-FSM input-driven sparsity at runtime by compressing the active-state set into a compact bitmap and skipping computation for inactive automata entirely.
th: sparsity-driven automata processing acceleration

t: Klotski: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference via Expert-Aware Multi-Batch Pipeline
pb: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs with trillion-scale parameters must be offloaded to CPU/disk memory when GPU VRAM is insufficient, but each expert's compute time per token is shorter than the I/O time to load it, creating large pipeline bubbles that negate the benefit of overlapping I/O and computation.
me: Klotski introduces an expert-aware multi-batch pipeline that maintains multiple batches in flight simultaneously and schedules which experts to prefetch and compute based on expert routing decisions across batches. By batching tokens that activate the same expert across multiple concurrent requests, Klotski increases per-expert compute volume to exceed I/O time, eliminating pipeline bubbles. The system tracks expert access patterns across batches and uses an expert prefetching scheduler that co-optimizes I/O and compute assignment to saturate both the memory bus and compute units.
nv: An expert-aware multi-batch pipeline for MoE offloading that batches tokens across multiple concurrent requests routed to the same expert to amortize I/O cost and eliminate pipeline bubbles.

mx.other: pipeline bubble reduction for offloaded MoE inference

th: multi-batch expert-aware scheduling for offloaded MoE inference

t: MetaSapiens: Real-Time Neural Rendering with Efficiency-Aware Pruning and Accelerated Foveated Rendering
pb: Point-Based Neural Rendering (PBNR), particularly 3D Gaussian Splatting, is computationally too expensive to run in real time on mobile devices due to the large number of Gaussian primitives and the full-resolution rendering required.
me: MetaSapiens combines two techniques: (1) efficiency-aware pruning that reduces the number of Gaussian primitives based on their contribution to rendering quality, using a pruning criterion that accounts for both visual importance and computational cost on the target hardware; and (2) accelerated foveated rendering that exploits the human visual system's reduced acuity in peripheral regions by rendering the foveal region at full quality and peripheral regions at lower resolution or with fewer Gaussians, reducing total computation. Both techniques are co-designed with the mobile hardware execution model to maximize throughput.
nv: Co-designing efficiency-aware Gaussian pruning with hardware-targeted foveated rendering to achieve real-time PBNR on mobile devices.

mx.other: not stated in abstract; claims real-time PBNR on mobile devices

th: efficiency-aware pruning and foveated rendering for mobile neural rendering

t: FSMoE: A Flexible and Scalable Training System for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Models
pb: Existing MoE training systems (DeepSpeed-MoE, Tutel) support only limited routing functions and use fixed or heuristic pipeline degrees, leaving significant communication overhead because they fail to overlap inter-node AlltoAll dispatch/combine with intra-node ESP-AllGather/ESP-ReduceScatter communications, and do not co-design Gradient-AllReduce scheduling with MoE-layer communication.
me: FSMoE introduces three techniques: (1) a modular abstraction dividing each MoE layer into six sub-modules (Gate, Order, I-Order, Dispatch, Combine, Expert) with hooks for non-invasive customization, plus a two-phase front-end/back-end profiler-scheduler that fits linear performance models for GEMM and collective operations; (2) a three-stream pipeline schedule that co-schedules intra-node ESP-AllGather/ReduceScatter with inter-node AlltoAll Dispatch/Combine and expert computation by classifying execution into four cases (dominated by inter-node comm, expert compute, AlltoAll, or intra-node comm) and using SLSQP to find the optimal pipeline chunk degree r for each case; and (3) an adaptive gradient partitioning method that slices Gradient-AllReduce work and assigns chunks to overlappable windows within and across MoE layers via a two-step algorithm (greedy assignment then differential evolution optimization), decoupling forward and backward pipeline degrees.
nv: The first MoE training system to simultaneously overlap both inter-node (AlltoAll) and intra-node (ESP-AllGather/ReduceScatter) communications with computation via adaptive per-phase pipeline degree selection, combined with MoE-aware adaptive Gradient-AllReduce partitioning.

mx.speedup: 1.18x-1.22x over Tutel+PipeMoE on 1458 MoE layer configs; 1.19x-3.01x over DeepSpeed-MoE on GPT-2/Mixtral real-world models
mx.other: up to 1.42x speedup on individual gating function benchmarks vs DeepSpeed-MoE; performance model fitting r^2 >= 0.9999 for all collective types

th: Adaptive communication-computation pipeline scheduling for sparse MoE training

t: Neuralink: Fast on-Device LLM Inference with Neuron Co-Activation Linking
pb: On-device LLM inference on smartphones using sparsity-based techniques (loading only active neurons from flash) suffers from excessive random I/O operations due to scattered neuron placement in flash, and smartphones face severe IOPS constraints that make these I/O patterns a critical bottleneck.
me: Neuralink reorganizes neuron placement in flash storage offline based on neuron co-activation patterns: neurons that are frequently activated together are linked contiguously in flash, enabling sequential read access that is orders of magnitude more efficient than random IOPS on mobile flash. An online stage then uses tailored data access and caching strategies aligned with the sequential layout and hardware characteristics of the target phone. The two-stage pipeline (offline co-activation profiling and layout reorganization; online cache-friendly sequential access) reduces I/O operations for sparsity-based LLM inference.
nv: Offline neuron co-activation analysis to reorder flash storage placement so that frequently co-activated neurons are contiguously stored, converting random I/O patterns into sequential reads on mobile flash.

mx.speedup: 1.49x average end-to-end latency improvement over SOTA

th: Flash storage layout optimization for sparse on-device LLM inference

t: Pipirima: Predicting Patterns in Sparsity to Accelerate Matrix Algebra
pb: Sparse accelerators struggle with load imbalance when processing compressed sparse matrices due to unpredictable non-zero value distributions, limiting performance despite sparsity optimization opportunities.
me: Pipirima predicts non-zero value patterns in sparse matrices using resource-friendly simple counters inspired by branch predictors. During streaming of CSR-compressed matrices, predictor anticipates non-zero locations to enable proactive acceleration. Evaluated on SpMV and SpMM kernels.
nv: Pattern-prediction approach using simple counters to anticipate non-zero locations and mitigate load imbalance in sparse accelerators.
th: Pattern prediction for sparse matrix acceleration

t: Maximizing Energy Efficiency in Spiking Neural Networks: A Dynamic Joint Pruning Framework
pb: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) face energy and computational efficiency challenges due to growing architectural complexity, requiring aggressive pruning that balances multiple sparsity dimensions simultaneously.
me: A dynamic joint pruning framework combines multi-stage masking for fine-grained neuron firing threshold control, temporal attention batch normalization (TABN) with learnable time scaling, and a dynamic sparse strategy that adjusts importance coefficients based on real-time SOP (synaptic operation) computational impact.
nv: First framework to jointly optimize spatiotemporal spike sparsity and weight sparsity dynamically, minimizing synaptic operations in SNN inference.

mx.other: 126.38× SOP compression ratio on CIFAR-10

th: Dynamic joint pruning of spatiotemporal and weight sparsity for energy-efficient SNN inference

t: An Input-Aware Sparse Tensor Compiler Empowered by Vectorized Acceleration
pb: Sparse tensor computations (especially sparse matrix-matrix multiplication) suffer from poor performance due to rigid sparse formats and limited compiler support for diverse sparsity patterns. Existing tensor compilers offer limited sparse optimizations, forcing practitioners to choose between manual kernel design (high effort) and generic code generation (suboptimal performance).
me: SpMMTC analyzes the non-zero distribution of input sparse matrices at compile time and generates vectorized kernels optimized for the specific sparsity pattern. The compiler adapts to hardware ISA capabilities (SIMD width, cache hierarchy) and creates specialized SpMM kernels without manual tuning. Vectorization guidance and pattern-aware unrolling maximize hardware utilization.
nv: Input-aware sparse tensor compiler that analyzes runtime sparsity patterns and auto-generates vectorized kernels for SpMM without manual per-matrix optimization.

mx.speedup: 1.21–2.97× vs. TACO/TVM/ASpT; 1.52× for sparse MobileNetV1 inference

th: Input-aware vectorized compilation for efficient sparse tensor operations

t: Hydra: Harnessing Expert Popularity for Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference on Chiplet System
pb: Mixture-of-Expert (MoE) models suffer from extensive all-to-all communication between tokens and expert replicas across chiplets, as well as redundant computations in softmax gating for underutilized experts. These bottlenecks degrade performance and energy efficiency on distributed chiplet architectures.
me: Hydra employs a popularity-aware expert mapping strategy in software: routing tokens to experts based on expected gating distribution to minimize all-to-all communication volume. In hardware, it uses Content Addressable Memory (CAM) to eliminate explicit token permutation operations (replacing expensive SpMM unscrambling) and introduces a redundant-calculation-skipping softmax engine that bypasses unnecessary exponential/division for low-probability experts.
nv: Hardware-software co-design that exploits expert popularity (non-uniform gating) through popularity-aware mapping and CAM-based permutation avoidance, combined with selective softmax computation.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 169.1× power reduction vs. GPU, 18.9× vs. MoE accelerator

th: Chiplet-based MoE inference accelerator exploiting expert popularity for efficient communication and computation

t: BEVSA: A Real-Time Bird's-Eye-View Semantic Segmentation Accelerator for Multi-Camera System
pb: Bird's-eye-view (BEV) semantic segmentation for multi-camera systems (MCS) requires expensive view transformation (68.3 ms on edge devices) and exhibits high input activation sparsity (69.1%), resulting in low throughput and high latency unsuitable for real-time 3D perception.
me: BEVSA is a specialized hardware accelerator with two key innovations: (1) block-decomposed hierarchical BEV pooling that partitions search space in MCS-suitable ways, achieving 43.2x speedup over edge computing for BEV transformation, and (2) coarse-to-fine-grained zero-skipping convolution that handles both channel-level and tile-level sparsity, improving convolution throughput 1.61x. Implemented at 28nm, it targets edge deployment.
nv: Hardware acceleration of BEV pooling with hierarchical decomposition and adaptive sparsity-aware convolution for real-time multi-camera semantic segmentation.
th: Hardware-efficient BEV semantic segmentation via pooling and sparsity optimization

t: Espresso: Exploiting the Sparsity Property in Event Sensors with Spatiotemporal Ordering
pb: Event-based vision sensors generate sparse high-speed event streams, but efficient stream processing without destroying sparsity properties is architecturally challenging.
me: Espresso designs an FPGA-based architecture for event-based vision that efficiently processes spatiotemporal event streams while maintaining sparsity. Uses ordered data structures and specialized compute patterns to avoid materializing dense representations.
nv: FPGA architecture for sparse event stream processing that preserves sparsity throughout computation.
th: Sparse event stream processing via FPGA

t: LEMOE: LLM-Enhanced Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Microarchitecture Exploration
pb: Design space exploration for processor microarchitecture is challenging due to vast design space and multiple competing metrics; traditional algorithm-driven approaches cannot effectively incorporate expert domain knowledge.
me: Uses LLM to enhance implicit Bayesian model for multi-objective optimization; features program-aware warm-up phase utilizing LLM and LLVM to produce initial design set with rich prior knowledge; leverages LLM contextual learning to improve surrogate modeling under sparse data.
nv: LLM-enhanced Bayesian optimization framework that uses LLM contextual learning to improve surrogate models and sampling efficiency for microarchitecture DSE.
th: LLM-enhanced Bayesian optimization for microarchitecture design space exploration

t: A Cross-model Fusion-aware Framework for Optimizing (gather-matmul-scatter)s Workload
pb: Modern sparse and irregular neural networks (RGCN, SpConv, MoE) rely on gather-matmul-scatter workloads, but existing optimizations lack cross-model transferability, require expensive search, and cannot handle dynamic inputs efficiently.
me: Efficient-GMS proposes a fusion-aware framework with dataflow analysis to identify shared patterns and four optimized dataflow variants using vertical/horizontal fusion. A performance model predicts execution efficiency to reduce search space, and a lightweight heuristic selects optimal dataflow based on input characteristics and hardware.
nv: Cross-model fusion-aware dataflow patterns that transfer optimizations across RGCN, SpConv, and MoE without model-specific retuning.
th: cross-model gather-matmul-scatter optimization framework

t: SSpMV: A Sparsity-aware SpMV Framework Empowered by Multimodal Machine Learning
pb: Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication performance varies significantly across matrices and architectures; existing SpMV libraries use fixed algorithms that do not adapt to matrix sparsity patterns and hardware characteristics.
me: SSpMV integrates expert-designed features with multimodal neural network representations to predict the best-performing SpMV algorithm and parameters. MM-Adapter is a multimodal network capturing diverse computational feature modalities of SpMV (pattern, density, structure).
nv: Multimodal machine learning approach for adaptive SpMV algorithm selection that combines expert features with learned modalities.
th: multimodal machine learning for adaptive SpMV selection

t: VSpGEMM: Exploiting Versal ACAP for High-Performance SpGEMM Acceleration
pb: Sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) is fundamental in deep learning and scientific computing, but sparse matrices require compact storage and produce irregular memory access patterns, creating communication and computation bottlenecks. Existing accelerators struggle with storage format overhead and intermediate product merging.
me: VSpGEMM is a hardware accelerator on Xilinx Versal ACAP exploiting AI Engines (AIEs) and programmable logic (PL). Introduces BCSX (block-wise compressed storage format) enabling fixed-pattern memory access for both row-major and column-major data. Employs multi-level tiling decomposing SpGEMM into hierarchical granularities fitting AIEs. Uses hybrid AIE/PL partitioning to orchestrate intermediate product merging, reducing memory utilization and communication demand.
nv: BCSX block-wise storage format with multi-level tiling and hybrid AIE/PL orchestration for efficient SpGEMM on heterogeneous ACAP platforms.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 33.62× energy efficiency vs cuSPARSE on RTX 4090

th: high-performance SpGEMM acceleration on heterogeneous Versal ACAP via block-wise storage and hybrid dataflow

t: ReMaP: Macro Placement by Recursively Prototyping and Periphery-Guided Relocating
pb: Macro placement in chip floorplanning directly impacts timing (WNS/TNS) and dataflow efficiency, but expert-quality placement is time-consuming to generate. Existing macro placers lack structured approaches to place macros near periphery while optimizing dataflow and avoiding overlaps.
me: ReMaP uses a two-phase approach: ABPlace (angle-based analytical method) arranges macros along an ellipse capturing both dataflow optimization and overlap avoidance, producing rough periphery-aligned distributions. Follow-up heuristic positions macros along chip boundaries, mimicking expert practice. Recursive refinement improves placement quality iteratively. Parameter autotuning via search optimizes tool knobs.
nv: Angle-based analytical placement (ABPlace) combined with periphery-guided relocation, recursively applied to match expert macro placement practices.

mx.speedup: 34.15% WNS improvement, 65.39% TNS improvement, 8.75% from autotuning

th: expert-mimicking macro placement via angle-based analytics and periphery-guided relocation

t: Grasp: Group-based Prediction of Activation Sparsity for Fast LLM Inference
pb: ReLU-fied LLMs (ReLU-based activations enabling sparsity) can skip computation in MLPs with predicted zero activations, but existing sparsity prediction methods suffer from reduced prediction accuracy when dealing with distribution outliers, limiting skipping efficiency and speedup.
me: Grasp is a magnitude-based, training-free sparsity prediction technique building on sign-bit methods for ReLU-fied LLMs. It groups vector elements considering their value distribution within the vector and explicitly handles statistical outliers, allowing more accurate per-element impact estimation. The method efficiently identifies zero activations to enable memory access and computation skipping.
nv: Group-based magnitude prediction with explicit outlier handling for improved activation sparsity prediction in ReLU-fied LLMs.

mx.speedup: 1.85× speedup vs dense inference; 11% higher prediction accuracy
mx.other: higher skipping efficiency enabling memory access skipping

th: group-based sparsity prediction for accelerating ReLU-fied LLM inference

t: A Cutting-Edge Parallel Solver for Scalable Power Grid Analysis Using Nested Domain Decomposition
pb: Modern power distribution networks at sub-5nm nodes contain billions to trillions of nodes with reduced noise margins and high power density, creating massive sparse linear systems that conventional domain decomposition methods cannot solve efficiently due to exponentially growing dense Schur complements.
me: Proposes nested domain decomposition solver incorporating parallel Schur complement computation strategy and intermediate Schur complement to reduce the size of the final global Schur complement. The intermediate complement breaks the computation into manageable stages.
nv: Introduction of intermediate Schur complement in nested domain decomposition to reduce global Schur complement size and improve parallel scalability.
th: Nested domain decomposition for scalable power grid analysis

t: HiSpTRSV: Exploring Tile-Level Parallelism for SpTRSV Acceleration on FPGAs
pb: Sparse Triangular Solve (SpTRSV) in sparse BLAS is a critical level-2 kernel with inherent data dependencies; existing FPGA accelerators focus only on intra-tile parallelism, missing inter-tile parallelism opportunities due to challenges in dependency graph construction, communication overhead, and workload balancing.
me: HiSpTRSV designs tile-based highly parallel algorithm leveraging inter-tile parallelism through dependency graph parsing, tile-based parallelization, filtering mechanisms, and bidirectional matching with modular indexing to handle communication overhead and workload distribution.
nv: First FPGA accelerator for SpTRSV exploiting inter-tile parallelism beyond intra-tile computation, addressing communication and workload balance challenges.

mx.speedup: 3.58x vs. GPU, 34.3% vs. SOTA SpTRSV accelerator

th: FPGA-based sparse triangular solver with inter-tile parallelism

t: ELF: Efficient Logic Synthesis by Pruning Redundancy in Refactoring
pb: Logic optimization via refactoring incurs high computational cost; conventional cut-based refactoring fails to improve circuit 98% of the time on average, wasting computation.
me: ELF uses a machine-learning classifier to preemptively prune unsuccessful cut candidates before expensive resynthesis operations. Classifier predicts which cuts are unlikely to yield improvements, eliminating wasted computation. Applies to ABC logic synthesis framework's refactor operator.
nv: ML-based cut pruning to eliminate redundant refactoring operations before resynthesis.
th: ML-accelerated logic synthesis via cut pruning

t: BitPattern: Enabling Efficient Bit-Serial Acceleration of Deep Neural Networks through Bit-Pattern Pruning
pb: Bit-serial DNN accelerators struggle with unstructured bit sparsity, causing workload imbalance and inefficient memory access due to irregular non-zero bit distributions.
me: Algorithm-hardware co-design: (1) algorithm level identifies optimal bit-pattern combinations via pruning, applies compression encoding for weight storage, merges similar patterns for workload balancing; (2) hardware implements bit-serial accelerator with dedicated pattern decoder and PE exploiting structured bit-pattern sparsity. Pattern-based approach vs bit-level irregularity.
nv: Structured bit-pattern pruning to convert unstructured bit sparsity into hardware-friendly regular patterns.
th: Pattern-based bit sparsity for bit-serial accelerators

t: DenSparSA: A Balanced Systolic Array Approach for Dense and Sparse Matrix Multiplication
pb: Existing sparse matrix acceleration architectures incur heavy area/power overhead, undermining efficiency for dense workloads; systolic arrays excel at dense but struggle with sparse matrices.
me: DenSparSA augments classic systolic array with compact sparsity-handling circuits for unstructured sparse matrices; uses circuit gating to disable sparsity overhead during dense operations; supports both single-side and dual-side sparse multiplications.
nv: Minimal-overhead sparsity extension to systolic arrays via decoupled circuit modules and gating.
th: Balanced systolic array for dense-sparse matrix multiplication

t: PacTrain: Pruning and Adaptive Sparse Gradient Compression for Efficient Collective Communication in Distributed Deep Learning
pb: Distributed DNN training is bottlenecked by gradient aggregation overhead; existing gradient compression schemes fail to accelerate training while preserving accuracy.
me: PacTrain actively prunes DNN weights (sparsifying gradients); performs lightweight adaptive compression using known global sparsity patterns; integrates with allreduce primitive for compatibility with distributed training frameworks.
nv: Combines pruning and adaptive gradient compression to achieve near-optimal compression while remaining allreduce-compatible.
th: Adaptive sparse gradient compression for distributed training

t: SynGPU: Synergizing CUDA and Bit-Serial Tensor Cores for Vision Transformer Acceleration on GPU
pb: Vision Transformers suffer from quadratic time/memory complexity in self-attention, leading to inefficiency on GPUs despite token pruning methods overlooking bit-level sparsity.
me: Proposes Inter-token Bit-sparsity Awareness (IBA) algorithm exploring bit-sparsity from similar tokens. SynGPU enables GPU implementation via Bit-Serial Tensor Core (BSTC) supporting fixed- and floating-point MMA, with novel data mapping to enable full CUDA/Tensor Core parallelism.
nv: Bit-Serial Tensor Core combining fixed-point BSDP and floating-point exponent alignment for efficient bit-sparse transformer compute.

mx.other: 2.49-3.81x compute density vs A100

th: Bit-level sparsity exploitation for efficient vision transformer inference on GPU

t: SSFT: Algorithm and Hardware Co-design for Structured Sparse Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
pb: Sparse fine-tuning (SFT) reduces time and memory requirements compared to dense fine-tuning, but GPU implementation underperforms due to irregular sparse data access patterns that modern GPUs cannot efficiently handle, negating computational benefits.
me: SSFT-Alg introduces predictable sparsity patterns reducing memory access overhead and enhancing regularity. SSFT-Hw accelerator optimizes SSFT-Alg with sparsity-aware design avoiding GPU sparse overhead. Co-design balances algorithm structure and hardware capabilities.
nv: Structured sparsity patterns designed specifically for hardware implementation, enabling efficient acceleration without generic sparse operation overhead.

mx.speedup: 51.0x vs GPU, 1.32x vs SOTA sparsity accelerators

th: Structured sparse fine-tuning with hardware-algorithm co-design for LLMs

t: High-throughput Point-Cloud Accelerator with Sparsity-aware Hierarchical Neighbor Voxel Search and Skipping
pb: 3D sparse convolution networks for point cloud processing face challenges from irregular voxel sparsity patterns, increasing hardware complexity and reducing efficiency when exploiting sparsity.
me: Algorithm-hardware co-design approach combining on-the-fly threshold-based voxel skipping at the algorithm level with a hierarchical 3-stage Voxel Search and Skipping engine at the hardware level to systematically narrow down the non-zero search space and adapt to irregular sparsity.
nv: Hierarchical multi-stage voxel search pipeline that adaptively narrows the search space based on sparsity, combined with on-the-fly threshold-based skipping to reduce computational waste.

mx.other: 77.7% delay reduction vs baseline

th: Hierarchical sparsity-aware point cloud 3D convolution accelerator

t: An Efficient Bit-level Sparse MAC-accelerated Architecture with SW/HW Co-design on FPGA
pb: Bit-level sparsity exploitation for MAC units is a proven efficiency improvement, but FPGA implementations face architectural limitations; existing FPGA designs lack effective bit-level sparsity support compared to ASIC value-aware accelerators.
me: Software/hardware co-design solution introducing LUT-friendly encoding with adaptable granularity that maps efficiently to FPGA LUTs, combined with hardware supporting multiplication time uncertainty to handle variable-latency sparse operations. This approach balances redundancy elimination with accuracy preservation and FPGA compatibility.
nv: LUT-friendly variable-granularity encoding scheme enabling bit-level sparsity exploitation on FPGAs while maintaining timing closure and accuracy.
th: LUT-friendly bit-sparse MAC accelerator on FPGA

t: Bit-Separable Transformer Accelerator Leveraging Output Activation Sparsity for Efficient DRAM Access
pb: Transformer inference is memory-bound; DRAM bandwidth limits throughput, especially for attention operations where memory access patterns are irregular.
me: The accelerator uses bit-separable representation for sparse activations, compressing output activations to reduce DRAM traffic. It combines this with specialized access patterns optimizing for sparse memory reads/writes.
nv: Bit-separable sparse activation encoding reducing DRAM bandwidth for transformer inference.
th: Sparse-activation-aware transformer accelerator

t: Bit-slice Architecture for DNN Acceleration with Slice-level Sparsity Enhancement and Exploitation
pb: Existing bit-slice DNN accelerator architectures exploit sparsity only at coarse granularity — either input or weight sparsity independently — failing to simultaneously leverage both input and weight sparsity at fine (bit-slice chunk) granularity, leaving substantial computational savings unrealized.
me: BADA (Bit-slice Architecture for DNN Acceleration) introduces a front-end unit that generates bit-slices from operands and selectively gathers only non-zero slices using a packed-nonzero selection mechanism, forwarding them to a back-end signed MAC unit. The architecture skips computation for (a) bit-slice chunks containing all zeros (coarse-grained) and (b) any operand pair where either input or weight bit-slice is zero (fine-grained joint sparsity). Two algorithmic optimizations complement the hardware: (1) a novel 8-bit data bit-slice representation with no additional hardware overhead (vs. 6-7 bit limits in prior work); (2) a training-time weight distribution narrowing technique that increases the proportion of zero-valued higher-order bit-slices, enhancing slice-level weight sparsity.
nv: Joint exploitation of both input and weight sparsity at the bit-slice chunk granularity using a front-end non-zero selection unit, combined with a training-aware weight distribution narrowing to amplify higher-order slice sparsity.
th: Joint input-weight bit-slice sparsity exploitation for DNN acceleration

t: EXION: Exploiting Inter-and Intra-Iteration Output Sparsity for Diffusion Models
pb: Diffusion model inference requires up to 1000 denoising iterations through transformer blocks (dominant 38-100% of operations), resulting in excessive energy consumption and latency; existing transformer accelerators target only QKV projection and attention computation within a single iteration and do not exploit the iterative structure or the dominant FFN layer overhead.
me: EXION is a SW-HW co-designed diffusion accelerator exploiting two types of output sparsity. First, the FFN-Reuse algorithm identifies temporal data redundancy across iterations in FFN GELU outputs: one dense iteration is computed fully, then N sparse iterations reuse the GELU output for low-magnitude elements (achieving 70-97% sparsity in the 1st FFN layer, reducing FFN ops by 52-85%). Second, an improved eager prediction algorithm using two-step leading-one detection (TS-LOD) predicts attention scores via log-domain approximation to identify and skip negligible attention computation within each iteration (20-95% intra-iteration sparsity, skipping avg. 26% Q and 22% KV projections). The ConMerge data compaction mechanism converts resulting unstructured sparse output matrices into compact dense forms via column condensing (removing all-zero columns) and block merging (merging sparse and dense tiled blocks using conflict-vector tracking). The dedicated hardware Diffusion-Sparsity Aware Core (DSC) contains: a Sparse-Dense Unified Engine (SDUE) with a 16x16 DPU array with per-DPU input/weight/conflict-vector switches enabling flexible ConMerge-aware dataflow; a ConMerge Assistant Unit (CAU) with sparsity-level sorting and ConMerge vector generation; an Eager Prediction Engine (EPRE) with TS-LOD-enhanced log-domain DPU array; and a Configurable SIMD Engine (CFSE) for special functions. Synthesized at 14nm, 800MHz, 0.8V.
nv: FFN-Reuse: the first algorithm exploiting temporal data redundancy in FFN GELU outputs across diffusion iteration steps to create inter-iteration output sparsity, combined with a ConMerge hardware mechanism that converts unstructured output sparsity into compact matrices executable at high utilization.

mx.speedup: 3.2-379.3x over RTX 6000 Ada (server GPU); 42.6-1090.9x over Jetson Orin Nano (edge GPU); 5.2x vs Cambricon-D on DiT
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 45.1-3067.6x energy efficiency over server GPU; 196.9-4668.2x over edge GPU
mx.area: EXION24 (24 DSCs + 64MB GSC): 152.28mm2 vs. RTX 6000 Ada 609mm2
mx.accuracy: Negligible accuracy loss across 7 models (FFN-Reuse: zero accuracy impact; EP+TS-LOD: minimal PSNR/FID degradation)
mx.other: FFN-Reuse: 52-85% FFN op reduction; ConMerge: 77.4%->8.4% remaining cols (Stable Diffusion); CAU area: 0.94% of DSC

th: Inter- and intra-iteration output sparsity exploitation for diffusion model acceleration via FFN-Reuse and ConMerge

t: SparseWeaver: Converting Sparse Operations as Dense Operations on GPUs for Graph Workloads
pb: Real-world graph workloads have sparse and skewed adjacency structures that cause severe warp-level load imbalance on GPUs, where existing software or hardware balancing schemes incur memory overhead or excessive inter- and intra-warp synchronization cost.
me: SparseWeaver is a hardware-software co-design that converts sparse graph operations into balanced dense operations by exploiting graph topology. A lightweight GPU functional unit microarchitecture called Weaver is added to GPU cores; it analyzes common sparse-to-dense conversion patterns identified via static/dynamic analysis and implements the conversion directly in the execution pipeline, leveraging memory access locality without additional synchronization. The design is prototyped on the open-source RISC-V Vortex GPU.
nv: Converting sparse graph operations to dense ones at the hardware level using a dedicated Weaver functional unit that exploits topology-driven patterns, eliminating the memory and synchronization overhead of prior software balancing schemes.

t: CROSS: Compiler-Driven Optimization of Sparse DNNs Using Sparse/Dense Computation Kernels
pb: Exploiting DNN weight sparsity on GPUs is hindered by the overhead of index-based encoding/decoding required by sparse formats, making sparse computation kernels slower than dense kernels even at high sparsity ratios.
me: CROSS is an end-to-end compilation framework that analyzes parameter distribution locality to identify regions where dense computation remains efficient. It decomposes sparse DNN workloads into multiple components across different sparsity levels and maps each component to either a specialized sparse kernel or a high-performance dense kernel. A novel sparse graph translation technique transforms the sparse computation graph into a form compatible with dense computation kernels, reconciling the sparse DNN computation with optimized BLAS-level dense routines on GPU. The framework accommodates various sparsity patterns (unstructured, structured, N:M) and optimization techniques.

Hardware support for sparsity must simultaneously deliver high bandwidth utilization and computational efficiency.

At the micro-architecture level, TB-STC implements a Transposable Block-wise N:M Sparse Tensor Core with an adaptive codec for on-the-fly storage format conversion supporting both row-wise and column-wise sparse access, and an I/O-aware configurable scheduler for sparsity-aware compute scheduling. t: Prosperity: Accelerating Spiking Neural Networks via Product Sparsity
pb: Existing SNN accelerators exploit bit sparsity (zero-valued spikes) to skip zero multiplications, but this approach leaves substantial redundancy unexploited: non-zero spike patterns that produce structurally identical inner products across matrix rows are recomputed independently, wasting significant compute.
me: Product Sparsity is a new sparsity paradigm that identifies combinatorially similar binary spike patterns across matrix rows: if two rows share identical non-zero positions, their dot products with the same weight vector are identical and only one needs to be computed, with the result reused for the other. Prosperity implements this via a real-time pattern matching engine that groups rows by their spike pattern hash, computes the inner product once per unique pattern, and distributes results to all matching rows. This is applied to both fully-connected and convolutional layers of SNNs with binary activations.
nv: Product Sparsity: a novel combinatorial sparsity paradigm that reuses inner product results across matrix rows with matching binary spike patterns, achieving far higher effective sparsity than bit-level zero-skipping alone.

t: A Hardware-Software Design Framework for SpMV Acceleration with Flexible Access Pattern Portfolio
pb: Sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) is difficult to accelerate due to highly irregular data access patterns that vary by input matrix structure. Static accelerators optimized at compile time cannot handle the dynamic matrix structures encountered in large practical SpMV workloads.
me: SPASM is a hardware-software co-design framework that extracts local data access patterns from input matrices and derives a portfolio of template patterns to encode matrix tiles. A reconfigurable hardware computing structure supports vectorized computation and flexible run-time switching between different template patterns per tile. Global composition analysis of input matrices drives hardware configuration and workload scheduling to improve load balancing across parallel processing units. The template portfolio can be optimized for expected input sets while retaining flexibility for unseen patterns.

t: HSMU-SpGEMM: Achieving High Shared Memory Utilization for Parallel Sparse General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on Modern GPUs
pb: Hash-based SpGEMM algorithms on GPUs fail to simultaneously minimize hash collisions and efficiently utilize fast shared memory, causing significant performance degradation when executing sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication.
me: HSMU-SpGEMM introduces a novel accumulator design that maximizes shared memory utilization on modern GPUs by rethinking the hash-based accumulation strategy to reduce collision overhead while packing more active data into shared memory. The approach also optimizes the symbolic stages of SpGEMM (row count, product computation) to complement the new accumulator. Evaluation is performed on three GPU microarchitectures (Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Turing).

t: AccelES: Accelerating Top-K SpMV for Embedding Similarity via Low-bit Pruning

Two novel sparse matrix storage formats, Ultra-CSR and Random-CSR, are introduced to optimize memory bandwidth utilization for irregular access patterns inherent in SpMV. The low-bit approximation in Stage 1 filters out irrelevant entries early, reducing the volume of full-precision computation dramatically.

t: Transitive Array: An Efficient GEMM Accelerator with Result Reuse
pb: General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) in DNNs and LLMs incurs high computational cost and memory bandwidth demand, especially in resource-constrained deployments. Existing quantization and sparsity methods reduce precision but do not exploit reusable intermediate partial results within GEMM computation.

An optimal DAG execution order is determined to resolve dependency and parallelism constraints. The Transitive Array accelerator exploits this sparsity through a multiplication-free design that distributes work across multiple parallel lanes for balanced throughput.

t: Telos: A Dataflow Accelerator for Sparse Triangular Solver of Partial Differential Equations
pb: Sparse triangular solve (SpTRSV) dominates runtime in preconditioned iterative solvers for PDE-derived linear systems due to loop-carried dependencies that severely limit parallelism. A plane-parallel pipelining technique maps dependent computations across processing elements (PEs) while preserving data locality within each plane. A cross-plane communication aggregation technique reorganizes inter-plane data transfers into systolic flows, enabling pipelined resolution of loop-carried dependencies with minimal stall overhead. t: HYTE: Flexible Tiling for Sparse Accelerators via Hybrid Static-Dynamic Approaches

me: HYTE is a hybrid static-dynamic tiling framework for sparse accelerators. An offline static scheduler first samples the sparse matrix to estimate a near-optimal initial tiling configuration — covering tile size and shape, dimension iteration order across tiles, and buffer allocation policies — without analyzing the full tensor. At runtime, a dynamic tuning mechanism adjusts tile shape on-the-fly to maintain high buffer utilization as local sparsity patterns vary. HYTE also manages tiling metadata in both off-chip memory and on-chip buffer efficiently, handling the non-negligible metadata overhead that prior sparse tiling schemes neglect.

t: Phi: Leveraging Pattern-based Hierarchical Sparsity for High-Efficiency Spiking Neural Networks
pb: Spiking Neural Network (SNN) accelerators exploit binary activation sparsity (0-1 spikes) to skip zero computations, but they ignore the structured distribution patterns present in spike activations, leaving significant compute savings unexploited. Existing designs treat each non-zero spike independently, incurring redundant runtime multiply-accumulate operations.
me: Phi introduces a two-level hierarchical sparsity framework for SNNs. Level 1 is vector-wise sparsity: spike activations are represented using a small set of pre-defined patterns selected offline via k-means clustering, enabling offline pre-computation of pattern-weight products so that most runtime multiply-accumulates are eliminated. Level 2 is element-wise sparsity: a highly sparse residual matrix (the complement of the Level 1 approximation) handles remaining activations, further reducing computation while preserving accuracy. A pattern-aware fine-tuning technique is applied to increase Level 2 sparsity. The Phi hardware architecture processes both levels on-the-fly, with dedicated datapaths for each sparsity tier.

t: Bishop: Sparsified Bundling Spiking Transformers on Heterogeneous Cores with Error-constrained Pruning
pb: Spiking transformers combine attention mechanisms with spike-based computation, but their large size and high spatiotemporal volume of computation make efficient hardware acceleration difficult due to variable activation sparsity and the inefficiency of treating attention's binary spike operations with conventional accelerator designs.
me: Bishop introduces the Token-Time Bundle (TTB) container that groups spike data across tokens and time steps for efficient packing. A heterogeneous accelerator routes high-density TTBs to a dense core array and low-density TTBs to a sparse core array via a stratifier. BSA (Bundle Sparsity-Aware) training improves structured TTB-level firing sparsity. ECP (Error-Constrained TTB Pruning) trims spiking query/key/value activations with a provable error bound before and after attention map computation. A reconfigurable TTB spiking attention core executes attention as AND-and-Accumulate operations on binary spikes.

t: RTSpMSpM: Harnessing Ray Tracing for Efficient Sparse Matrix Computations
pb: Sparse matrix-matrix multiplication (SpMSpM) is a critical kernel for graph analytics, GNNs, and scientific computing, but existing GPU SpMSpM libraries underutilize hardware because the irregular memory access and conditional computation patterns of sparse data do not map well to standard GPU CUDA cores and tensor units.
me: The authors first observe the algorithmic analogy between SpMSpM (identifying non-zero output positions) and ray-triangle intersection (finding ray-geometry intersections), then implement SW-RTSpMSpM — an SpMSpM algorithm mapped to the standard ray tracing API (DXR/OptiX) that uses RT core intersection units for non-zero position detection. Analysis of the differences between the two algorithms motivates RT+SpMSpM, which introduces two architectural optimizations: (1) simultaneous computation of partial products alongside RT intersection tests (not just detection), and (2) a ray mapping and scheduling strategy paired with a small row accumulation engine (RAE) that exploits Gustavson's sparse row-by-column dataflow and eliminates reliance on shader fallbacks and redundant memory operations. The RAE introduces only 0.2% area overhead on a modern high-end RT GPU.
nv: Mapping SpMSpM as a ray tracing problem and then proposing targeted architectural extensions (simultaneous multiply with intersection + row accumulation engine) that boost efficiency while adding only 0.2% area to an existing RT-equipped GPU.

t: Quartz: A Reconfigurable, Distributed-Memory Accelerator for Sparse Applications
pb: Sparse tensor and graph workloads exhibit irregular memory access patterns and variable computation densities that defeat fixed-dataflow ASIC accelerators designed for dense workloads. The architecture exposes a programmable dataflow substrate that can be configured at runtime to match the access pattern of a given sparse kernel. Distributed memory banks reduce the bandwidth bottleneck by providing high aggregate internal bandwidth close to the compute units. A reconfigurable interconnect routes data between memory banks and processing elements according to the configured dataflow.

t: SeaCache: Efficient and Adaptive Caching for Sparse Accelerators
pb: Sparse tensor accelerators suffer from poor on-chip SRAM utilization because variable-length sparse fibers (rows/columns of nonzero data) do not map cleanly into fixed-size cache blocks, wasting capacity. Theoretically optimal replacement policies (e.g., Belady OPT) require expensive on-chip metadata that consumes significant die area.
me: SeaCache combines three techniques targeting sparse on-demand caches integrated in domain-specific accelerators. First, fiber packing and splitting maps variable-length sparse fibers into fixed-size cache blocks with high utilization by splitting long fibers across multiple blocks and packing short fibers together. Second, a practical replacement policy approximates OPT-like behavior at low implementation cost by exploiting access-pattern regularities in sparse computations. Third, an adaptive space-sharing mechanism dynamically partitions the cache between actual data and replacement policy metadata using a two-phase approach that measures and adjusts the optimal partition ratio at runtime.

t: A Probabilistic Perspective on Tiling Sparse Tensor Algebra
pb: Tiling sparse tensor algebra computations for cache efficiency is challenging because the effective tile size and cache behavior depend on the sparse data distribution, which varies across inputs and is not known at compile time.
me: The paper takes a probabilistic approach to sparse tensor tiling, modeling the sparsity pattern probabilistically to predict cache behavior and guide tile-size selection. Specific mechanism details are not available from the abstract alone.
nv: A probabilistic framework for analyzing and selecting tile sizes in sparse tensor algebra that accounts for input-dependent sparsity patterns.
th: probabilistic tiling optimization for sparse tensor algebra

t: Bootes: Boosting the Efficiency of Sparse Accelerators Using Spectral Clustering
pb: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (SpGEMM) accelerators using row-wise product dataflow suffer from poor off-chip memory traffic because row reordering — the primary technique to improve data reuse — is either suboptimal, slow to compute, or fails to detect when reordering is counterproductive for certain sparsity patterns.
me: Bootes applies spectral clustering to reorder rows of the input matrix A before feeding them into a row-wise SpGEMM accelerator. A similarity matrix capturing structural properties of A's row sparsity patterns guides the clustering; similar rows are placed adjacent so that their accesses into B have high overlap, maximizing data reuse. The spectral clustering algorithm itself is optimized to reduce preprocessing time to a geometric mean of 11.61x faster than existing reordering techniques. A decision tree model trained on real-world sparse matrices predicts whether reordering will be beneficial before executing it, enabling cost-aware preprocessing that avoids overhead when reordering would increase traffic.
nv: Using spectral clustering on a row-similarity matrix to optimally reorder SpGEMM inputs for maximum off-chip data reuse, combined with a decision tree gating mechanism to skip reordering when it is counterproductive.

mx.other: Off-chip traffic reduction: 2.31x (Flexagon), 1.67x (GAMMA), 1.38x (Trapezoid); preprocessing speedup: 11.61x geomean over prior reordering

th: Spectral clustering row reordering to minimize SpGEMM off-chip memory traffic

t: Misam: Machine Learning Assisted Dataflow Selection in Accelerators for Sparse Matrix Multiplication
pb: SpGEMM accelerators that support multiple dataflows (e.g., row-wise, column-wise, inner-product) face two critical problems: (1) no fast principled mechanism exists for selecting the optimal dataflow at runtime given input matrix sparsity patterns, and (2) providing hardware flexibility for multiple dataflows incurs area overhead and underutilization when one dataflow is locked in.
me: Misam uses a lightweight decision tree classifier to dynamically predict the optimal SpGEMM hardware configuration from matrix structural features (sparsity density, distribution, pattern statistics) extracted at runtime. To overcome hardware underutilization from multi-dataflow support, Misam targets FPGAs and exploits FPGA partial reconfigurability to deploy specialized, resource-efficient bitstreams tailored to specific sparsity regimes on demand. A reconfiguration engine evaluates whether the anticipated performance gain from switching bitstreams exceeds the reconfiguration overhead before triggering a reconfiguration.
nv: Using FPGA partial reconfiguration guided by a runtime ML decision tree to deploy sparsity-regime-specialized bitstreams on demand, achieving the efficiency of a fixed-dataflow accelerator with the adaptability of a flexible one.

mx.speedup: Up to 10.76x speedup via adaptive reconfiguration

th: ML-guided FPGA reconfiguration for adaptive SpGEMM dataflow selection

t: SparseTransX: Efficient Training of Translation-Based Knowledge Graph Embeddings Using Sparse Matrix Operations
pb: Training translational knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models (TransE, TransR, TransH, TorusE) is bottlenecked by fine-grained scatter/gather operations during gradient computation (up to 40% of CPU training time), causing irregular memory access patterns, high backpropagation overhead, and large intermediate memory allocations.
me: SparseTransX reformulates translational KGE training by constructing a sparse incidence matrix A from training triplets: each row represents one triplet, with +1 in the head entity column and -1 in the tail entity column (for ht expression) or additionally +1 in the relation column offset by entity count (for hrt expression). Multiplying A (sparse, M x (N+R)) by the embedding matrix E (dense, (N+R) x d) directly computes batched (head - tail) or (head + relation - tail) expressions via a single SpMM call. Both forward and backward pass benefit: backward reduces to SpMM on the transpose A^T. Four models implemented: TransE (hrt computation, L2 norm), TransR (ht computation + per-relation projection matrix Mr applied separately), TransH (two ht computations with hyperplane projections), TorusE (hrt with torus distance). Framework uses iSpLib (CSR format, SIMD vectorized, auto-tuned) for CPU and DGL g-SpMM (COO format) for GPU. PyTorch DDP/FSDP wrappers support distributed training.
nv: First application of SpMM to replace scatter-gather in translational KGE training; sparse incidence matrix formulation that unifies head-tail-relation embedding extraction into a single matrix multiplication enabling high-performance sparse library acceleration.

mx.cpu_speedup_transe: up to 5.3x speedup on CPU vs TorchKGE (across 7 datasets including BioKG 4.8M triplets)
mx.gpu_speedup_transe: up to 4.2x speedup on GPU vs TorchKGE
mx.gpu_memory_transh: 0.28 GB vs 3.1 GB (TorchKGE) for TransH (11x reduction)

th: sparse-computation-for-graph-ml

t: Distributed Submodular Subset Selection at Billion Scale
pb: Submodular subset selection for dataset pruning requires materializing all candidate points in a central machine's memory, making it infeasible at billion-point scale.
me: A distributed bounding algorithm partitions data across workers; each worker computes local upper/lower bounds on marginal gains using grow/shrink steps based on min/max utilities without requiring point-to-point communication. A multi-round partition-based greedy scheme with adaptive repartitioning aggregates global selections. Implemented on Apache Beam for large-scale distributed execution.
nv: Bounding algorithm that avoids centralizing data by computing provably tight bounds on submodular marginal gains in a distributed manner, enabling selection quality approaching centralized greedy without a central memory bottleneck.

mx.accuracy: 98% of centralized greedy quality at 32 communication rounds
mx.other: Scales to 13 billion points; adaptive partitioning reduces rounds needed

t: N:M Sparse DNN Kernels for RISC-V MCUs via Custom ISA Extension
pb: N:M semi-structured sparsity cannot be efficiently exploited on RISC-V microcontrollers (MCUs) because standard ISAs lack the hardware primitives to accelerate structured sparse operations without prohibitive overhead.
me: A custom xDecimate ISA instruction is added to a RISC-V core that performs hardware-accelerated N:M sparse selection and MAC in a single operation. Decimate Im2col reformulates convolution to enable xDecimate on im2col-transformed feature maps. The MATCH compiler generates xDecimate-aware kernels. Synthesized at 22nm targeting the Vega PULP SoC (basis for commercial GAP9). Evaluated on ResNet-18 and ViT at 1:4, 1:8, and 1:16 sparsity ratios.
nv: xDecimate: first RISC-V ISA extension specifically designed for N:M semi-structured sparsity, enabling hardware-level acceleration of 1:4 through 1:16 sparse patterns at only 5% area overhead on a commercial-grade SoC.

mx.other: 1:4 and 1:8 sparsity also evaluated with proportionally lower speedups

t: Dynamic Input Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference on Mobile Devices
pb: SwiGLU-based LLM MLP layers on mobile devices are memory-bandwidth bound, with all weight matrices (up, gate, down projections) fully loaded from DRAM for every token, causing excessive energy consumption and low throughput.
me: Dynamic Input Pruning (DIP) applies predictor-free top-K selection on MLP input activation magnitudes, selecting only the K largest input elements and pruning corresponding columns of the up, gate, and down projection matrices. No separate predictor network is needed. LoRA adapters can be added for fine-tuning recovery. DIP-CA (cache-aware variant) uses a gamma multiplier (gamma=0.2) to bias selection toward cached weight columns, reducing DRAM refetch. Evaluated via simulation of Apple A18 (60 GB/s DRAM, 1 GB/s Flash) on Phi-3-Medium, LLaMA models.
nv: Predictor-free input-magnitude-based dynamic pruning of all three SwiGLU MLP matrices simultaneously, with a cache-aware variant (DIP-CA) that coordinates column selection with hardware memory hierarchy to maximize DRAM reduction.

t: Efficient On-Device Machine Learning with a Biologically-Plausible Forward-Only Algorithm
pb: Backpropagation-based DNN training on IoT and wearable edge devices is infeasible due to excessive memory (activations must be stored), energy consumption, and biologically implausible requirements (weight transport, non-locality, update locking, frozen activities).
me: Bio-FO trains each layer independently using only forward passes. For each hidden layer l, an auxiliary classifier with a fixed random matrix Bl projects layer activations hl to class predictions, computing local cross-entropy loss and gradient without backpropagating through other layers. Weight updates use only local activations (hl-1 and hl), avoiding weight transport (no symmetric backward weights), non-locality (no inter-layer error signals), update locking (updates proceed as activations arrive), and frozen activities (no activation storage required). A sparsity mask Sl enables locally connected (LC) and CNN extensions. Implemented in PyTorch; evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, medical EEG/ECG datasets, and mini-ImageNet on NVIDIA Jetson Nano.
nv: First forward-only algorithm to simultaneously and fully address all four biological implausibility issues of BP (weight transport, non-locality, update locking, frozen activities) while outperforming prior forward-only methods (FF, PEPITA, DRTP) in accuracy and achieving 3x memory reduction and up to 19.8x energy reduction.

t: Enabling Unstructured Sparse Acceleration on Structured Sparse Accelerators
pb: Unstructured sparse DNN models cannot be accelerated on structured sparse hardware (e.g., 2:4 NVIDIA sparse Tensor Cores), and structured sparse models require hardware-specific fine-tuning making them non-portable.
me: TASD (Tensor Approximation via Structured Decomposition): decomposes any sparse tensor into a series of N:M structured sparse tensors using the distributive property of tensor algebra. TASD-W performs offline weight decomposition via greedy layer-wise search minimizing dropped non-zeros while maintaining 99% model quality. TASD-A handles dynamic runtime activation decomposition with sparsity-degree-based pattern selection attached to accelerator input. TTC (TASD Tensor Core) extends VEGETA/STC to support multiple N:M patterns simultaneously. Decomposition-aware dataflow keeps B/C tiles stationary to amortize the decomposition overhead.
nv: First method enabling unstructured sparse DNNs to run on structured sparse hardware without fine-tuning, via tensor series decomposition exploiting the distributive property of matrix algebra.

mx.speedup: 39% speedup on NVIDIA RTX 3080 (2:4 sparse Tensor Cores)

mx.accuracy: Maintains 99% model quality target with greedy decomposition

t: Self-Data Distillation for Recovering Quality in Pruned Large Language Models
pb: Structured depth pruning of LLMs removes decoder blocks and reduces compute, but post-pruning SFT causes catastrophic forgetting by shifting the data distribution away from the original model's knowledge.
me: Angular cosine distance between adjacent block outputs is used to identify which layers are most redundant (lowest angular distance = most similar outputs = best pruning candidates). The unpruned model then rewrites the fine-tuning dataset: for each prompt, the unpruned model generates a 'distilled' response that preserves semantic richness. Conditional selection keeps original responses for prompts where the pruned model already performs acceptably. SLERP model merging blends pruned and distilled model checkpoints. The pruned model is also used as a speculative decoding draft model paired with the full model as verifier.
nv: Using the unpruned model to regenerate a semantically-aligned distillation dataset for post-pruning SFT, preventing catastrophic forgetting while maintaining the efficiency of depth pruning; plus SLERP merging and speculative decoding as downstream applications.
hw: GPU inference (A100-class); edge deployment of pruned models
th: Model Compression & Pruning

t: COMET: Fine-grained Computation-communication Overlapping for Mixture-of-Experts
pb: In distributed MoE models, inter-device all-to-all communication occupies up to 47% of total execution time. Existing coarse-grained overlapping schemes impair computational efficiency and provide sub-optimal latency concealment.
me: COMET introduces two mechanisms: (1) Shared Tensor Based Dependency Resolving: analyzes the shared buffers between producer (communication) and consumer (computation) operations, decomposes shared tensors along independent dimensions (M-axis for layer0 GEMM, N-axis for layer1 top-K reduction), and reschedules computation tiles to begin as early as possible using local data first. (2) Adaptive Workload Assignment: thread-block specialization isolates communication and computation in separate SM groups within a fused kernel, with adaptive thread-block allocation profiled per input shape and parallelism strategy.
nv: Fine-grained fused GPU kernels that resolve the granularity mismatch between token-level communication and tile-level GEMM computation through shared tensor decomposition and rescheduling, combined with adaptive SM allocation that dynamically balances communication vs. compute SMs at runtime.
th: MoE Communication Optimization / Kernel Fusion

t: Bridging the Gap between Unstructured SpMM and Structured Sparse Tensor Cores
pb: Sparse-dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) on Tensor Cores is inefficient for unstructured sparse matrices due to low block-wise density, causing computational waste. Specialized Sparse Tensor Cores (SpTCs) require strict 2:4 or 1:2 structured sparsity, creating a mismatch with real-world unstructured sparse data.
me: MP-SpMM: A Matching and Padding approach inspired by graph theory's maximum matching problem to transform unstructured sparse matrices into structured sparsity patterns compatible with SpTCs. Includes novel storage format and highly optimized GPU kernel.
nv: Graph-theory-inspired matching algorithm that converts arbitrary sparse patterns to SpTC-compatible structured sparsity without excessive padding; optimized GPU kernel exploiting SpTC capabilities for unstructured inputs.

t: StraGCN: GPU-Accelerated Strassen's Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication for Graph Convolutional Network Training
pb: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) suffer from high computational cost during training due to inefficient Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM), limiting scalability and throughput.
me: GPU-accelerated SpMM using Strassen's algorithm with three key optimizations: (1) horizontal fusion model for kernels improving shared memory locality, (2) intermediate result reuse exploiting adjacency matrix immutability, (3) two-stage matrix partitioning to balance load irregularities from sparse structure.
nv: First practical GPU-accelerated Strassen SpMM implementation specifically optimized for GCN training, combining algorithmic improvements with GPU architecture-aware optimizations.

t: FaSTCC: Fast Sparse Tensor Contractions on CPUs
pb: Sparse tensor contractions are a core computational primitive in scientific computing and machine learning, but effective optimization through loop permutation/tiling remains an open challenge. Uses probabilistic modeling to automatically select between dense/sparse output tile accumulators and determine optimal tile sizes. Implements hashing-based parallel execution.

t: KDRSolvers: Scalable, Flexible, Task-Oriented Krylov Solvers
pb: Sparse linear solver frameworks (PETSc, Trilinos) are inflexible in data partitioning; changes to partitioning strategies require extensive code refactoring and don't automatically propagate.
me: Abstract sparse matrix representation using dependent partitioning that maps between domain, range, and nonzero entries. Universal co-partitioning operators for matrices and vectors. Multi-operator systems enable non-contiguous data processing. Targets Legion task-based runtime system.
nv: First abstraction to decouple sparse matrix storage format from Krylov algorithm implementation; automatic partitioning strategy propagation; multi-operator data ingestion.
th: Flexible sparse linear solvers via abstraction-based partitioning

t: Enabling Unstructured Sparse Fine-Tuning and Inference for Foundation Models on Wafer-Scale Engine
pb: Foundation models fine-tuned on dense weights don't benefit from sparse pre-training; dense fine-tuning negates sparsity savings, requiring full-precision inference despite underlying sparse structure.
me: Phoenix merges sparse pre-trained weights with low-rank adapters during fine-tuning. Preserves sparsity structure while adapting to downstream tasks. Leverages Cerebras CS-2 unstructured sparsity support for efficient inference.
nv: First method to maintain sparsity during fine-tuning via sparse-weight + low-rank adapter merging; enables 50–60% sparsity on Cerebras without accuracy loss.
th: Sparse inference for fine-tuned foundation models on wafer-scale
